03Case study 01

Centro Napoletano
di Ortodonzia

Sector
Healthcare / Orthodontics
Duration
9 months
Channels
Instagram · Facebook
Location
Naples, Italy

The brief

  • Family-run orthodontic centre, Naples, since 1978. Run today by the founder's three daughters.
  • Strong clinical reputation, weak digital presence.
  • Goal: rebuild online presence around three generations of family trust, to reach a new generation of parents.

Result: one verified, in-person conversion after 7–8 months of consistent publishing, traced back to Facebook.

Full case study

What the strategy included

Buyer personas

Three detailed personas built around real fears and needs: Elena (prevention-first new mum), Chiara (pragmatic, cost- and time-driven), Luca (17, aesthetics-driven, TikTok-first).

The mistake I caught

I focused on the target audience without studying the centre's specific services in enough depth, so the strategy and the content plan drifted apart. Now I always map services before planning content.

Content pillars

Value-driven posts on generational trust, educational content on early prevention, and structured copy built around each persona's real pain points.

Concrete, verifiable goals

13 organic posts in the first month, then structured monthly targets instead of vague promises.

The lesson

You can't expect immediate conversions from communication that's still building awareness. Real results take time, and I now say that clearly to clients from day one.

The strategy document itself, built in Notion:

04Case study 02

Just Play
Salerno

Sector
Youth retail / streetwear
Duration
3 months
Channels
Instagram · TikTok · Facebook
Location
Salerno, Italy

The brief, and a complication

  • Streetwear store network (Nike, Jordan, Adidas, Vans, Dickies), ages 0–16.
  • Salerno store open under a year. Instagram account largely inactive.
  • Introduced an empathy map, and visited the store in person instead of trying to learn every brand's technical detail.

Result: 4,705 views on the top Reel in month one, reached organically with zero paid promotion — the clearest reach numbers among the three case studies here. Content also began surfacing under organic search terms like "sneakers" and "abbigliamento".

Full case study

Strategic decisions

  1. Built two opposite buyer personas, the pragmatic mum and the trend-aware 13-year-old, so the content could speak to both without alienating either.
  2. Proposed a hybrid content model: dynamic, aspirational visuals for TikTok, practical and informative stories for Instagram.
  3. Structured the content funnel at 50% awareness, 35% trust, 15% sales, and never promised immediate purchases from a dormant profile that was only just restarting.

The lesson

Good technical work isn't enough if you don't also manage the client's expectations on realistic timelines. I've deliberately worked on that skill since.

More proof

Screenshot: top Reel and best post.

Early signs of discoverability

Within the first month, content started surfacing under search terms like "sneakers" and "abbigliamento", not just reaching existing followers. That's the platform correctly reading the profile as a clothing store and pushing it to people actively searching those terms, a small but concrete sign the awareness strategy was working.

05In-house role

Goeldlin

Sector
Fashion / Workwear
Role type
In-house, not freelance
Duration
5 months
Channels
Instagram · Facebook
Location
CIS di Nola, Italy

The brief

  • Workwear manufacturer, CIS di Nola. First in-house role, full company, not freelance.
  • Built a new Instagram strategy from zero. Target: +15% brand awareness in 6 months.
  • Audit found a large share of existing followers were fake or bought.
  • Proposed rebuilding the profile from zero. The client said no.

Result: reporting metric switched from follower count to reach and engagement.

Full case study

What I found, and the call I made

The follower count didn't add up

Early on, I checked the account's audience quality and found that a large share of the existing followers were fake or bought, most likely from before I joined. The engagement numbers made no sense next to a following that size.

I proposed starting clean

I suggested closing the profile and rebuilding it from zero, so every future number would reflect a real, engaged audience. The owner said no: for him, the follower count did its job as social proof for buyers deciding whether to order workwear from Goeldlin.

The lesson

I kept working with what I had, and focused my reporting on the metrics that were still honest: reach, interactions, and views on the content I published, not the follower count. Sometimes the job isn't managing a client's data, it's telling them their asset is worth less than it looks, and being ready for them to say no anyway. That's why you won't find growth percentages on this slide. I'd rather show you the decision than a number I don't fully trust. It's also the moment that taught me the most about my own gaps at the time, and shaped how I run every strategy since.

06Current focus

Refining the method,
not chasing new clients

Since January 2026, no paying clients. Instead: the same strategy process I run for clients, applied to my own page, one level deeper than before.

Full process, applied to myself
Personal brand knowledge · Buyer personas · Market positioning · Competitor analysis & SWOT · Market offer · SMART goals · Communication strategy

Empathy mapping, applied to myself

A technique from a previous client, turned on my own positioning. Harder without distance from the subject, but it forced content that isn't generic.

A monthly synthesis, before any content

One focus service, goals, and KPIs first. Micro-topics and communication angles follow, not the other way round.

Content matched to profile phase

A dormant profile isn't ready for sales content. Awareness first, offer later, so strategy and content stay coherent.

A live lab to fix my own method, plus continued courses and study, before applying it for someone else again. That's the workflow shown in the next section.
